<!--
Shared Typst styling for the one-page class summaries (`class/N-stub/summary.qmd`).

This is the single source of truth for how every summary PDF looks. Include it
right after the YAML header of a summary.qmd with Quarto's include shortcode,
pointing at `../_summary-styles.qmd`. (Not written out literally here — Quarto
expands shortcodes even inside HTML comments, so an example would make this file
include itself forever.)

Then open the sheet with the header banner and switch to two columns:

    ```{=typst}
    #summary-header(1, "Getting Started", "August 26, 2026")
    #show: rest => columns(2, rest)
    ```

Everything below is raw Typst: `#let` bindings and `set`/`show` rules defined
here stay in scope for the rest of the document, since Quarto concatenates all
`{=typst}` blocks into one .typ file.

Authoring note: don't pack symbol-only inline code into a middot-separated run
(`` `#` `` · `` `-` `` · `` `1.` ``). At 7.5pt the symbols are indistinguishable
from the separators and it reads as a rendering failure. Use a two-column table
instead. Middot runs are fine for lists of *words* (software names, dates).
-->

```{=typst}
// ---- Palette (mirrors class/_extensions/lexis/lexis.scss) --------------------
#let accent = rgb("#E74A2F")   // $color-red
#let ink    = rgb("#121212")   // $color-black
#let muted  = rgb("#5f5f5f")
#let hairline = rgb("#d8d8d8")
#let wash   = rgb("#f2f2f2")
#let codeink = rgb("#2c8475")  // $color-darkgreen, matches inline code on slides

// ---- Base text --------------------------------------------------------------
#set text(font: "Source Sans Pro", size: 8.6pt, fill: ink)
#set par(justify: false, leading: 0.52em, spacing: 0.62em)
#show link: set text(fill: rgb("#007bff"))

// Code. Careful here: Quarto's syntax highlighter emits every *token* as its own
// inline `raw()` and joins lines with `raw("\n")`, so a `#show raw.where(block:
// false)` rule that wraps tokens in a box silently destroys the line breaks in
// every code block. Only touch the font, never the layout.
#show raw: set text(font: "Fira Mono", size: 7.5pt)

// Code blocks come through Quarto's `Skylighting` helper (defined in the
// template preamble), which hardcodes a light-gray 8pt-inset block. Shadow it
// here with a tighter, on-brand version — a later top-level `#let` wins for
// every call after it, and all of ours come after.
#show raw.where(block: true): set block(fill: wash, inset: 5pt, radius: 2.5pt)
#let Skylighting(fill: none, number: false, start: 1, sourcelines) = {
  let lines = []
  for ln in sourcelines { lines = lines + ln + raw("\n") }
  block(
    fill: wash, width: 100%, inset: (x: 5pt, y: 4.5pt), radius: 2.5pt,
    stroke: (left: 1.5pt + rgb("#dcdcdc")),
    lines,
  )
}

// ---- Headings ---------------------------------------------------------------
// Level 1 = section header (colored rule). Level 2 = sub-header inside a section.
#set heading(numbering: none)
#show heading.where(level: 1): it => block(width: 100%, above: 1.0em, below: 0.5em, {
  text(font: "Fira Sans", size: 9.5pt, weight: 700, fill: accent, tracking: 0.4pt,
       upper(it.body))
  v(-0.55em)
  line(length: 100%, stroke: 0.6pt + accent)
})
#show heading.where(level: 2): it => block(above: 0.75em, below: 0.3em,
  text(font: "Fira Sans", size: 8.8pt, weight: 600, fill: ink, it.body))

// ---- Lists ------------------------------------------------------------------
#set list(marker: text(fill: accent)[•], indent: 0.35em, body-indent: 0.4em,
          spacing: 0.42em, tight: true)
#set enum(indent: 0.35em, body-indent: 0.4em, spacing: 0.42em, tight: true)

// ---- Tables -----------------------------------------------------------------
#set table(
  stroke: (x, y) => (top: if y == 1 { 0.6pt + hairline } else { none },
                     bottom: none, left: none, right: none),
  inset: (x: 3.5pt, y: 2.6pt),
  fill: (_, y) => if y == 0 { none } else if calc.even(y) { wash } else { none },
)
#show table.cell.where(y: 0): set text(font: "Fira Sans", weight: 600, size: 8.2pt)
#show figure: set block(above: 0.7em, below: 0.7em)
// Tables are reference material — a table split across a column break is worse
// than the whitespace you get from pushing the whole thing to the next column.
#show table: it => block(breakable: false, it)

// ---- Callout: the one thing to remember -------------------------------------
#let keypoint(body) = block(
  width: 100%, fill: rgb("#fdeeeb"), inset: 6pt, radius: 3pt,
  stroke: (left: 2.5pt + accent),
  text(size: 8.4pt, body),
)

// ---- Header banner ----------------------------------------------------------
#let summary-header(week, title, date) = block(width: 100%, breakable: false, {
  grid(
    columns: (1fr, auto),
    align: (left + bottom, right + bottom),
    {
      text(font: "Fira Sans", size: 7.4pt, weight: 600, fill: muted, tracking: 0.6pt,
           upper("EMSE 6035 · Marketing Analytics for Design Decisions · Fall 2026"))
      v(-0.55em)
      text(font: "Fira Sans", size: 19pt, weight: 700)[Week #week: #title]
    },
    text(font: "Fira Sans", size: 7.8pt, fill: muted)[#date],
  )
  v(-0.35em)
  line(length: 100%, stroke: 1.8pt + accent)
  v(0.2em)
})

// ---- Page footer ------------------------------------------------------------
#set page(footer: context {
  set text(font: "Fira Sans", size: 7pt, fill: muted)
  line(length: 100%, stroke: 0.4pt + hairline)
  v(0.1em)
  grid(
    columns: (1fr, auto),
    align: (left, right),
    link("https://madd.seas.gwu.edu/2026-Fall/")[madd.seas.gwu.edu/2026-Fall],
    [#counter(page).get().first() / #counter(page).final().first()],
  )
})
```
